placeKinds:
Everyday places someone who lives there goes to, mixed across the neighbourhoods, each worth a conversation and no kind twice: a café, a market stall, a fonda or cocina económica, a taquería or street-food stand, a plaza or jardín, a church, a cantina or mezcalería, a practical shop (farmacia, papelería, tienda de la esquina), the bus terminal, and one or two places that are special to this city or where something is happening (a dance in the plaza, a workshop, a dig). No panaderías (Josh, 2026-10-27: "the conversation is poor"). At least one person with something to show: a scholar, a priest, a museum guide, a professor, a journalist, an archaeologist.

Who is where: at a business, someone who works there (the owner fits too). Customers, students and passers-by only in public places, never in a shop with nothing to sell. Every person has a reason to be at their place today (the `here` line). Kinds: one name per kind, lowercase, the same across cities ("café", "market", "bus-terminal", "church", "plaza").
placePrompt: Linocut print with bold carved black lines and wood-grain texture, in bright colour, of [the place, by name], [neighbourhood], [city], today. [What it looks like and who is there, one or two lines]. Bold colour: [two or three colours]. Square format, 1200 × 1200 pixels.

placeStyles.ciudad-de-mexico: The {neighbourhood} quarter of Mexico City as it really looks today, with its own architecture, street trees and everyday street life. Photorealistic city street photography, taken at eye level from a few steps back with nothing blocking the view: crisp detail, true-to-life saturated colour, bright late-morning sun and dappled light; no haze, no pastel wash, no deep dark shadows
placeStyles.guadalajara: Linocut print with bold carved black lines and wood-grain texture, strong contrast, in bright colour. Palette: terracotta, teal, mustard and sky blue
placeStyles.oaxaca: Mexican shadow-box diorama painted as naive folk art: the scene built inside a small open wooden box, with tiny handmade clay and papier-mâché figures and objects, every surface painted in bright saturated colours with careful small details and alebrije patterns, flat perspective, photographed straight on with soft light. Palette: cochineal red, marigold, indigo and turquoise
placeStyles.puebla: Illustration in the style of a hand-painted Talavera tile panel from Puebla: slightly glossy glaze, visible brush marks, a thin decorative tile border. Palette: cobalt blue and white with touches of yellow, ochre and green
placeStyles.san-miguel-de-allende: Mexican mural painting style: flat fresco look, simplified forms, strong rhythmic composition, matte plaster texture. Palette: terracotta, ochre, rose, slate blue and deep green
placeStyles.guanajuato: Mexican modernist easel painting, in the tradition of the painters born in this region: bold simplified forms, solid volumes, rich earth and jewel colours, visible brushwork on canvas. Palette: ochre, terracotta, emerald, cobalt and warm yellow
placeStyles.veracruz: 35 mm colour film photography taken at eye level: natural film grain, hard tropical light, a little sea haze in the distance, true colour with warm highlights; candid, unposed
placeStyles.patzcuaro: Etching with hand-tinted watercolour: fine black etched lines and cross-hatching, with soft washes of colour laid over them, on cream paper. Palette: lake blue, adobe white, roof red and pine green
placeStyles.merida: Watercolour on rough paper with fine ink outlines, light and airy, strong tropical sun. Palette: Mérida’s pastel colonial walls, ochre, rose, pale lime and white
placeStyles.san-cristobal-de-las-casas: Two-colour risograph print in indigo and warm red on off-white paper: solid, confident areas of ink with crisp edges, light grain only, slight misregistration between the two inks, flat overlapping shapes

placeRules: No other words anywhere: no dates, no 'HOY', no neighbourhood or city names, no slogans, no prices, no brand names or logos. Contemporary Mexico: today's clothes and objects, everyday life; no sombreros, skulls, rebozos or costumes. Keep the main scene in the centre; nothing important near the edges.
placeStylesNote: Chosen 2026-10-14 by Josh from the style test (content/es-mx/style-test.json). Each place prompt = city style + the place's scene (its imagePrompt) + its name as the only sign + placeRules (scripts/lib/place-prompt.mjs). The five cities added 2026-11-09 (Guanajuato, Veracruz, Pátzcuaro, Mérida, San Cristóbal) have styles proposed by the cloud session from each city's own craft or look, not yet tested: Josh judges one picture per city first. Veracruz's first idea, a silkscreen travel poster, was dropped as touristy (2026-11-09) for the port's hand-painted sign and boat style. Portraits stay in the one Mexican gouache style (Josh: "mexican portraits are great"). Revised the same night (Josh: the more successful Mexican images were Mexico City, San Miguel and Guadalajara, picture-making techniques rather than the scene rendered as a craft object like Oaxaca's diorama and Puebla's tiles): Guanajuato modernist easel painting, Veracruz 35 mm film photography, Pátzcuaro hand-tinted etching, San Cristóbal two-colour risograph; Mérida watercolour unchanged.

cityCards.guanajuato: Mexican modernist easel painting, in the tradition of the painters born in this region: bold simplified forms, solid volumes, rich earth and jewel colours, visible brushwork on canvas. Palette: ochre, terracotta, emerald, cobalt and warm yellow. Guanajuato today: houses in every colour stacked up the sides of a narrow ravine, the yellow dome of the basilica and church towers rising among them, the huge stone statue of El Pípila with his torch on the hill above. At the bottom, a city bus comes out of the stone arch of a tunnel under the town; students sit on a long flight of white stone steps; a woman carries shopping bags up a narrow stepped alley. Contemporary Mexico: today's clothes and objects, everyday life; no sombreros, cacti, skulls, rebozos, costumes or straw-hatted vendors, no sunset glow. Keep the main scene in the centre of the picture; nothing important near the top or bottom edges.
